subject: GX-7 Unit Cost Review and Supplier Decision

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Let's get into it. Renata sent around the updated cost model yesterday. Devon, you've had a chance to look at the Norrask quote versus what we're currently paying Veskell. Where do we stand?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: I've gone through both. Norrask is quoting us $18.40 per unit on the GX-7 main assembly at the volumes we're projecting for Q3 — that's five thousand units. Veskell is at $21.15 for the same volume, same spec sheet. The gap is meaningful.

turns.speaker: Renata
turns.text: To put that in dollar terms, at five thousand units we're talking about a $13,750 difference per run. If we do two runs before end of year, that's close to $28,000 in savings. That's not nothing.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: I want to understand what's behind Norrask's number before we get excited. Are they using the same board stackup? Because we had a conversation with them in November and they were pushing a six-layer instead of the eight-layer we spec'd.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Good catch. Their quote is based on the six-layer. I asked them specifically about the eight-layer and they came back at $20.90. So the apples-to-apples comparison is $20.90 Norrask versus $21.15 Veskell. That's a much smaller gap.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's almost nothing. Twenty-five cents a unit.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: So the headline number was misleading. Okay. Is there any reason to prefer Norrask on factors other than price?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Lead time is actually better with Norrask. They're quoting six weeks from PO to delivery. Veskell has been running eight to nine weeks, and they slipped us by two weeks on the last order. That cost us real pain on the Quennick fulfillment.

turns.speaker: Renata
turns.text: The lead time difference matters a lot if we're trying to hit the Q3 revenue target. Elena's been pushing for a July ship date on the Quennick expansion order, and two weeks of buffer is worth something.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: What's Norrask's yield history? Do we have any data on their defect rates? That's the thing I can't evaluate from a quote sheet.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: We don't have direct production data from them. They gave us a reference customer — a company called Brisquell Devices — but I haven't had a chance to call them yet. That's on my list.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: That reference call needs to happen before we make any commitment. Marcus, what would you need from a qualification standpoint if we did decide to switch?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: We'd want at least one pilot run of two hundred units, full inspection, and we'd need to see their process audit from the last twelve months. If they haven't had an external audit we'd want to arrange one, which adds time and cost.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Pilot run would probably cost us more per unit since it's below their minimum for the standard rate. They'd likely charge somewhere around $24 for a pilot batch.

turns.speaker: Renata
turns.text: So there's a qualification cost to factor in. Rough order of magnitude, if we do two hundred units at $24 that's $4,800 for the pilot, plus whatever the audit runs. We should model that against the $1,250 annual savings at current volumes.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: The payback math isn't compelling on price alone. Devon, what's your gut on Norrask operationally? You've visited their facility.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: I visited in October. The floor was clean, their SMT lines looked well-maintained, the operators knew their equipment. My gut is positive, but I've been wrong before. The reference call matters.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: I'd also want to know if they've built anything with our class of impedance-controlled traces. That's where we've seen problems with new vendors in the past.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Okay. Here's where I want to land. We don't switch suppliers based on a twenty-five cent per unit difference and no yield data. Devon, you make the Brisquell reference call and come back with what you learn. Marcus, can you write up the qualification criteria — what a new supplier would have to demonstrate before we'd commit volume to them?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: I can have that written up by end of next week.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: I'll get the reference call done by Friday.

turns.speaker: Renata
turns.text: Should I hold the Veskell relationship steady in the meantime? They've been asking about whether we want to lock in pricing for the full year.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Tell them we're evaluating options and we'll have an answer within thirty days. Don't commit to the year lock-in yet, but don't burn the relationship either.

turns.speaker: Renata
turns.text: Understood. One more thing — the cost model I circulated assumes the GX-7 BOM stays flat through Q4. Marcus, is that a safe assumption or are there component changes coming?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: There's a potential revision on the power management section. We've been looking at swapping the Kessendra PM-4 for the Tolvane equivalent because Kessendra lead times have stretched to sixteen weeks. If we make that swap it could affect the BOM cost by a dollar or two in either direction. I don't have a firm number yet.

turns.speaker: Renata
turns.text: Can you flag me when you have something more concrete? Even a range would help.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Will do. I'll know more after Sofia finishes the firmware compatibility check on the Tolvane part.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: All right. We're not making a supplier decision today. Devon calls the reference, Marcus writes up qualification criteria, Renata holds Veskell at arm's length for thirty days. Let's reconvene when Devon has the reference call results.

decisions: No supplier switch will be made until the Norrask reference call is complete and qualification criteria are established.
Veskell relationship to be maintained without a full-year pricing commitment for at least thirty days.

action_items.task: Call Brisquell Devices as a Norrask reference customer and report findings.
Write up formal supplier qualification criteria for new contract manufacturers.
Communicate to Veskell that a decision on year-long pricing lock-in will come within thirty days.
